findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a unit whose model call completes AFTER cancellation is observed is classified (committed success vs. cancelled vs. dropped) so AC3's 'exact completed/failed/cancelled accounting' has a well-defined cut point against non-interruptible in-flight calls.
evidence: pass1.py:226-228: 'In-flight runner calls are not interruptible; up to pool-width of them complete as sunk cost.'

AC3: 'the executor stops remaining work and returns exact completed, failed, and cancelled accounting without fabricating usage or findings' — silent on the classification of a unit whose model call completes AFTER the cancellation is observed.
Approach: 'cancellation observation' and 'cancellation abort remaining execution with exact completed-so-far accounting' do not define the completed-so-far cut point relative to in-flight calls.
findings.finding: The plan under-specifies how work that is in-flight-but-uncommitted at cancellation time is classified in the executor's outcome accounting. AC3 promises 'exact completed, failed, and cancelled accounting' on cancellation, but the existing runner documents that in-flight runner calls are not interruptible and complete as sunk cost after the cancel signal; the plan does not state whether such a late-completing unit is committed as success, recorded as cancelled, or dropped.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 3 (systemic/cancellation abort) and Approach ('cancellation abort remaining execution with exact completed-so-far accounting')
scenarios: A review is cancelled while N pool workers each have an outstanding provider call; those calls return valid content moments later — are they committed to the success/resume envelope or dropped?
Cancellation accounting must be 'exact' but the executor observes cancellation between scheduling and completion of an in-flight unit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the deterministic basis for budget shedding (e.g. shed in ascending unit-id order after dependency resolution) so the 'deterministically sheds' criterion is reproducible.
evidence: 'A positive explicit budget deterministically sheds work that does not fit'
'explicit positive-budget shedding, usage accumulation'
Absence: no stated ordering/priority for which units are shed first when the budget is exceeded
findings.finding: The shedding decision names 'deterministically sheds work that does not fit' but does not state the basis for determinism (e.g., unit id order, dependency/topological order, or estimate size) so two executors could shed different units for the same budget.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 4 / Approach ('explicit positive-budget shedding')
scenarios: Two units both fit individually but not together — which is shed is undefined
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the AC: 'shedding walks units in stable unit-id order and drops the first unit whose cumulative estimate exceeds the budget, then continues.'

evidence: 5 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the per-unit dependency graph / `skipped`-with-dependency-reason against a CURRENT done-definition unit that actually depends on another (cite it), or defer the dependency modeling until a dependent unit exists.
evidence: Approach: 'The executor owns dependency-aware scheduling ... a dependent of missing work becomes `skipped` with a dependency reason.'
AC2: 'marks dependent units skipped with the missing dependency id'
plan_review/pass1.py fans out chunks/agent criteria independently (ThreadPoolExecutor with per-future try/except); no inter-criterion dependency edges exist
code_review/batch_runner.py iterates `active_criteria` in a plain for-loop with no dependency handling
findings.finding: The plan introduces per-unit dependencies, dependency-aware scheduling, and a `skipped`-with-dependency-reason outcome, but neither current review gate has inter-unit dependencies: plan-review chunks criteria by facet and fans them out independently (plan_review/pass1.py), and code-review runs each overlay independently in a flat loop (code_review/batch_runner.py). No named done-definition includes a dependent unit, so the dependency graph and its skip path appear to serve a hypothetical rather than a current requirement (YAGNI / premature abstraction).
findings.location: Approach ("dependency-aware scheduling", "a dependent of missing work becomes `skipped`") + AC line 2
scenarios: A reviewer implements a full dependency DAG + skip-propagation that no criterion ever exercises, adding untested scheduling surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the concrete current criterion/unit pair that requires a dependency edge; if none exists today, drop dependencies + the `skipped`-dependency path from S2 and reintroduce them when a dependent unit lands.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document the legacy-checkpoint transition as an explicit choice with an expand-contract or back-out note (e.g. legacy envelopes are intentionally invalidated; cost is bounded re-execution; no dual-read is provided).
evidence: 'Legacy checkpoints are never read as new successes.'
'injected failed, cancelled, skipped, shed, corrupt, and legacy envelopes remain missing'
Absence: no migration, dual-read, or rollback path for the envelope-version cutover
findings.finding: The plan makes prior successful checkpoints unusable ('Legacy checkpoints are never read as new successes'; legacy envelopes 'remain missing') which forces re-execution of previously completed work, but states no expand-contract sequence or back-out path for this behavior change.
findings.location: Approach ('Legacy checkpoints are never read as new successes') / AC line 5
scenarios: A resumed review after this ships re-runs all criterion work because its stored checkpoints are the legacy format
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Boundaries note justifying legacy invalidation and confirming there is no dual-read migration, so the re-execution cost is a deliberate, reversible-by-revert decision.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the new shared discovery-kernel contract and outcome taxonomy in an ADR or design-doc/AGENTS.md update.
evidence: 'Add a narrow shared discovery kernel under rebar.llm.review_kernel'
'A focused execution kernel gives both gates the same trustworthy facts'
Absence: no ADR or design-doc capture named for the new kernel contract shared by two gates
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new shared discovery kernel and a new versioned checkpoint/trace contract consumed by both review gates — a novel cross-component architectural decision — but does not mention capturing it in an ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.
scenarios: A future author touching either gate needs to understand the kernel contract and outcome taxonomy

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the kernel's 'dependency-aware scheduling' relates to the existing executor.py graphlib.static_order scheduler + Burr tripwire (reuse it, or justify why per-unit scheduling must live in the kernel instead of the executor).
evidence: workflow/executor.py: 'runs a validated workflow's steps in graphlib.static_order (topological) order' and 'test_executor_tripwire.py reads THIS file and fails if [asyncio/concurrent/threading/... ] is imported, so the executor cannot silently grow a scheduler'
executor.py Burr-adoption trigger list (ADR 0065) explicitly gates 'non-linear control flow the static DAG can't express' and 'parallel step execution'
Boundaries claims to avoid 'a second workflow interpreter' but the Approach still asserts dependency-aware scheduling ownership in review_kernel
findings.finding: The plan's executor 'owns dependency-aware scheduling', but the repo already has a deliberately-thin workflow executor that runs steps in graphlib.static_order (topological) and carries an armed 'Burr tripwire' test plus ADR 0065 gating any growth of dependency/parallel scheduling. The plan's Boundaries disclaim 'building a second workflow interpreter' yet do not reconcile the new scheduler with the existing DAG executor or the tripwire, so the kernel risks rebuilding scheduling that already exists (NIH / second scheduler).
findings.location: Approach ("The executor owns dependency-aware scheduling") + Boundaries ("without building a second workflow interpreter")
scenarios: The kernel grows its own topological scheduler/DAG-order logic parallel to executor.py's graphlib.static_order, splitting scheduling across two modules.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drive the executor via the existing graphlib.static_order path (kernel supplies only outcome/checkpoint semantics), or add a Boundaries note reconciling the kernel scheduler with executor.py + ADR 0065 and confirming the tripwire is not violated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite the RP-01 prerequisite with a resolvable [rebar:<id>] token (or an edge in this ticket's deps) and name the concrete symbol/boundary the executor observes when a 'local operation' is exhausted, so the retain-and-continue seam is grounded.
evidence: Plan: 'After RP-01 exhausts a local operation it preserves successful independent results and continues; a dependent of missing work becomes skipped'
Plan: 'A focused execution kernel gives both gates the same trustworthy facts without ... fighting RP-01 provider semantics'
search_files for 'LocalOperation', 'def local_operation', and 'exhaust'/'operation' in operations.py & pass1.py -> (no matches)
show_ticket('RP-06') -> Error: Ticket 'RP-06' not found — no verifiable prerequisite edge
findings.finding: The plan leans on prerequisite 'RP-01' for a load-bearing execution seam ('After RP-01 exhausts a local operation it preserves successful independent results and continues'; 'fighting RP-01 provider semantics') but the reference is uncited (no [rebar:<id>] token) and unresolvable: show_ticket('RP-06') returned not-found, and no 'local operation'/exhaustion concept is grounded in operations.py or plan_review/pass1.py.
findings.location: Approach / Boundaries and Rationale ('After RP-01 exhausts a local operation...'; '...fighting RP-01 provider semantics')
scenarios: The 'preserve earlier successes and continue after a local failure' behavior (AC2) is defined only in terms of an RP-01 seam whose shape cannot be confirmed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the out-of-dir consumers (plan_review ProductionBatchRunner/run_pass1, code_review CodeReviewBatchRunner) and state whether each is rewired to drive the new executor or explicitly left unchanged in this ticket.
evidence: Plan: 'Both review gates execute criterion work through runners whose return values cannot reliably distinguish...'
code_review/batch_runner.py CodeReviewBatchRunner.run() loops criteria and calls agent_runner.run(ctx) directly
plan_review/production_batch_runner.py ProductionBatchRunner.run() calls run_pass1(...) which owns the shed/checkpoint loop (pass1.py load_checkpoint/save_checkpoint)
findings.finding: The plan states 'both review gates execute criterion work through runners' and defines 'the real executor' as the shared execution core (AC2/AC3), but does not enumerate the out-of-dir consumers a real integration must update: plan_review's ProductionBatchRunner + run_pass1 (which today own the dependency/budget/checkpoint loop) and code_review's CodeReviewBatchRunner (which today drives per-overlay agent runs directly).
scenarios: A reviewer estimating blast radius cannot tell whether ProductionBatchRunner/run_pass1/CodeReviewBatchRunner are rewired to call the new executor or left untouched.
